input.summary: The claim requires comparing TCP flow completion time at 0 ms vs. 20 ms additional delay using the built-in emulated-netem-v1 runner. Two key decisions remain unresolved before a complete protocol can be proposed: delay placement (one-way vs. round-trip) and the specific netem script/topology to use, which determines how many clients are required and what other fixed parameters apply.
clarification_questions: Is the 20 ms delay applied one-way (e.g., sender→receiver only) or round-trip (both directions)? The runner contract requires an explicit placement declaration — a value alone does not specify this.

Which netem script will be used for this pilot — netem_nines.py (requires exactly 2 clients), netem_cubic_benchmark_nines.py, or netem_cubic_benchmark_hotnets.py (both support 1–10 clients)? Please also supply the versioned source identity and SHA-256 digest of the script so it can be recorded in input_versions.

What fixed bottleneck parameters should be held constant across both conditions (e.g., bandwidth cap in Mbit/s, queue size, loss rate, transfer size or duration)? These must be specified to make the two conditions comparable.
